prompt: Use case: product-mockup. Asset type: a photorealistic PBR base-color texture atlas for an existing quadrotor drone mesh, NOT an image of a drone. Generate a landscape atlas, 1536 by 1024 pixels, divided into an exact 3-column by 2-row grid of six equally sized square material tiles. Tiles touch with NO gutters, NO labels, NO borders, NO perspective. Every tile is a flat orthographic material sample with neutral uniform diffuse lighting, no baked directional highlights or cast shadows. Top-left: light warm gray injection-molded polymer drone shell, very subtle fine realistic grain, mostly uniform, tiny understated manufacturing wear, no large markings. Top-center: dark graphite carbon-fiber composite with a realistic fine tight diagonal twill weave, restrained contrast, no glossy lighting gradients. Top-right: satin dark gunmetal aluminum for electric motor housings, finely machined linear grooves, subtle neutral metallic grain. Bottom-left: a realistic dark charcoal rectangular battery housing seen straight on, low-relief fine ribs, a small integrated four-dot green charge indicator near the top center, no readable text or branding; leave broad plain dark margin. Bottom-center: the frontal face of a compact drone optical camera, exactly centered circular deep black glass lens with restrained teal coated-glass color, concentric dark metal rings, set within a square matte dark charcoal camera housing filling the whole tile; circular lens occupies 65 percent of tile width. Bottom-right: very dark charcoal rubberized grip/landing-foot material, extremely fine pebbled texture, uniform and seamless-looking. Professional realistic materials with restrained detail at small scale. Do not add any entire drone, logos, watermarks, lettering, scenery, outer shadows, panels beyond the six exact tiles, or extra layout decorations. The six tiles will be mapped separately onto shell, arms/propellers, motors, battery, camera and landing gear of the existing model.
layout: Three columns, two rows: polymer shell, carbon composite, machined metal; battery, camera lens, rubber.
usage: Keep surface.json, albedo.png and surface_uv.npz together. Configure the matching Drone visual profile with surface: ${PROJECT_ROOT}/libraries/targets/appearances/uav_survey/surface.json. Enable texture maps in pygfx.
